scenes.headline: Where a ROS 2 depth node gets its metres
scenes.sub: Depth Anything 3 in TensorRT, and the one line that makes it metric
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Quartz! One camera measures direction, not distance. So when this ROS 2 node publishes depth in metres, who supplied the metres?

scenes.text: The network predicts depth as if the focal length were 300 pixels. The node multiplies in the camera's real focal, and the metres fall out.
scenes.mark: multiplies in the camera's real focal
scenes.say: The model predicts depth as if the focal length were three hundred pixels. The node multiplies in the real focal length, and metres fall out.

steps.say: Every frame is resized straight into a fixed grid, five hundred and four by two hundred and eighty.
Depth Anything 3 runs in TensorRT and emits raw depth and a sky map. The model file stops there.
A CUDA kernel takes the focal lengths from the camera's calibration message, scales every pixel into metres, and marks the sky.
Out come a point cloud on the network's own grid, and a full-size depth image.

parts.note: the camera's focal lengths, scaled to the network's grid
parts.say: Take both focal lengths, scaled to the network's grid, and average them.

parts.note: DA3's normalisation: depth as if the focal were 300 px
parts.say: Divide by three hundred, the focal length the model's depth assumes.

parts.note: applied to every pixel in the CUDA postprocess
parts.say: Multiply every pixel. No stereo, no known object: that's all the scale there is.

left.title: Depth image
items: Upscaled to full size, ringing at edges
left.say: The depth image is upscaled to full size, and fills the sky with a far depth, up to two hundred metres.

right.title: Point cloud
right.say: The point cloud stays on the network grid, and leaves the sky empty.

scenes.label: shorter distances on a 4:3 camera, from the node's stretch-and-average
scenes.note: exact only at 1.8:1; re-export at 504x378 to fix it
scenes.say: The catch: this is exact only for a one point eight to one frame. On a four by three camera, every distance comes out thirteen percent short.

scenes.text: A monocular depth node is only as metric as the calibration and the aspect ratio you feed it.
scenes.mark: only as metric as the calibration

recap: The model outputs depth normalised to a 300 px focal
One CUDA multiply turns it into metres
Exact at 1.8:1; re-export for other cameras
scenes.say: To recap: normalised depth from the model, metres from one multiply, and an aspect ratio to check first.
